 As Indian equity markets prepare to enter Samvat 2083 and gear up for Muhurat Trading, special one-hour trading session scheduled on Sunday, November 8, 2026, to mark Diwali Laxmi Pujan, several brokerages and research firms have identified stocks across different sectors, including banking, IT, defence, healthcare, hospitality, automobiles, consumer and industrial, that could offer investment opportunities over the coming year.
 Shriram Research, Sahi Research, Jainam and InCred Equities have picked their Diwali stock recommendations for Samvat 2083, highlighting companies with strong earnings potential, improving business fundamentals, attractive valuations and opportunities arising from India's domestic growth story.
 Where Indian equities stand this Diwali?
 According to Shriram Research, Samvat 2082 began on high expectations on the back of fiscal and monetary support from policymakers but closed with double-digit decline in several market segments amid global geopolitical tensions. Initially, tariff-related concerns weighed on investor sentiment, followed by geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, which disrupted energy supplies and pushed up crude oil prices. Higher energy costs also fuelled inflationary concerns and raised the possibility of tighter monetary conditions.
 However, domestic investors could take a longer-term view, supported by improving corporate earnings, favourable policy measures and an eventual improvement in global conditions. Shriram Research believes that Samvat 2083 could reward investors who tracks fundamental numbers rather than emphasising on daily market noise.
 “For investors, the new Samvat should therefore be about quality, patience and discipline. If inflation moderates, crude oil cools, earnings estimates improves then it will have positive impact on our relative valuations to global markets as a result foreign flows would start chasing value ideas on longer horizon,” it said.

 Shriram Research Diwali stock picks 2026: 11 stocks with upside potential of up to 32%
 Shriram Research has picked 11 stock, spanning banking, healthcare, consumer, industrial and automobile sectors, for Samvat 2083, with potential upside of up to 32 percent. These are:
 Aeroflex Industries: CMP Rs 514 | Target Price Rs 680 | Potential Upside 32%
 Dr. Lal Path Labs:  CMP Rs 1,887 | Target Price Rs 2,240 | Potential Upside 19%
 Eternal :  CMP Rs 344 | Target Price Rs 400 | Potential Upside 16%
 ICICI Bank:  CMP Rs 1,387 | Target Price Rs 1,620 | Potential Upside 17%
 Karur Vysya Bank:  CMP Rs 345 | Target Price Rs 418 | Potential Upside 21%
 Larsen & Toubro (L&T):  CMP Rs 3,940 | Target Price Rs 4,500 | Potential Upside 14%
 LG Electronics India:  CMP Rs 1,682 | Target Price Rs 1,950 | Potential Upside 16%
 Navin Fluorine International: CMP Rs 8,406 | Target Price Rs 10,080 | Potential Upside 20%
 Radico Khaitan: CMP Rs 4,100 | Target Price Rs 5,000| Potential Upside 22%
 Sona BLW Precision Forgings: CMP Rs 906 | Target Price Rs 1,000 | Potential Upside 10%
 Titan Company: CMP Rs 4,476 | Target Price Rs 5,250 | Potential Upside 17%
 Sahi Research Diwali stock picks 2026: Five stocks with buy ranges and targets
 Sahi Research has identified five stocks for Samvat 2083, providing specific buying ranges, stop-loss levels and price targets. The recommendations span defence technology, real estate, renewable energy, capital markets and banking.
 Zen Technologies: Buy range 1,700–1,740 | Stop Loss Rs 1,580 | Targets Rs 1,925 / 2,030
 DLF Ltd: Buy range 710–720 | Stop Loss Rs 620 | Targets Rs 790 / 880
 Adani Green Energy: Buy range 1,350–1,385 | Stop Loss Rs 1,165 | Targets Rs 1,590 / 1,800
 BSE Ltd: Buy range 3,590–3,640 | Stop Loss Rs 2,990 | Targets Rs 4,000 / 4,440
 HDFC Bank: Buy range 720–740 | Stop Loss Rs 620 | Targets Rs 815 / 870
 Jainam Diwali Muhurat Picks
 Jainam has identified five stocks across banking, hospitality, IT services and telecommunications, citing their business fundamentals, earnings prospects and growth opportunities. The recommendations include Indian Hotels Company, HDFC Bank , Kotak Mahindra Bank, Tech Mahindra and Bharti Hexacom.
 Indian Hotels Company: Hotels & Hospitality | Buy Rs 782 add Rs 700 | Target Rs 920 | Stop loss Rs 630 
 India’s largest hotel company (Tata group), with 390 operating hotels and 280 more in the pipeline across Taj, Vivanta, Ginger and other brands. “Growth is accelerating: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22% with occupancy at 82%, and management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 15–17%. 94% of the pipeline is asset-light, management fees grew 25% in Q2, and the company holds about Rs 1,500 cr of net cash with AAA ratings from ICRA and CARE,” it said. Key risks are a rich valuation (54.4x trailing P/E), West Asia disruption and a Rs 1,874 crore rent claim on the Taj Mahal Palace.
 HDFC Bank: Private Sector Bank | Buy Rs 693 add Rs 630 | Target Price Rs 850 | Stop loss Rs 562.50 
 India’s largest private bank, with about 14 percent of all bank loans, trades near decade-low valuations at 1.9x book and 14x earnings after a 30 percent fall in a year, even as FY26 profit grew 10.9 percent. Growth is back, with Q2 FY27 loans up 16.3 percent and deposits up 18.8 percent, largely closing the post-merger funding gap, said the brokerage.
 About 70 percent of loans are floating-rate and should reprice upward after the RBI hike, while asset quality stays pristine (gross NPA 1.11 percent, CET1 17.1 percent). Key risks are the leadership transition, NIM slipping to 3.16% and continued FII selling, it added.
 Kotak Mahindra Bank: Private Sector Bank | Buy Rs 430 add Rs 400 | Target Rs 520 | Stop loss Rs 352 
 Jainam said Kotak Mahindra Bank is a diversified financial group whose subsidiaries earned about Rs 5,280 cr in FY26, or 27 percent of group profit. “Growth is accelerating, with September 2026 loans up 24.7 percent and deposits up 23.2 percent year on year. Kotak has the highest NIM among large private banks (4.53%) and its benchmark-linked loans reprice quickly after the RBI hike. Asset quality is improving (gross NPA 1.18%, credit cost 46 bp), capital adequacy is 22.8%, and the Deutsche Bank India retail deal and a named new CEO add clarity. Key risks are a premium valuation (3.2x book), a weaker CASA ratio (40.3%) and the new ECL provisioning rules, it added.
 Tech Mahindra: IT Services | Buy Rs 1,790 add Rs 1,685 | Target Rs 2,150 | Stop loss Rs 1,480 
 The Project Fortius turnaround is delivering: EBIT margin has expanded for 12 straight quarters, from 6.1% in FY24 to 14.8% in Q2 FY27, and ROCE of 31.2% already meets the FY27 target. Q2 FY27 profit rose 32.7% on 7.2% constant-currency revenue growth, ahead of most large peers, and deal wins topped $1 bn for a fourth straight quarter. Shareholder payouts are strong, with a record Rs 51 FY26 dividend, an 85%+ free cash flow payout policy and a 1:1 bonus. Key risks are a 31.5x P/E against 14–22x for peers, 33.5% telecom concentration and AI-disruption fears, said the brokerage.
 Bharti Hexacom: Telecom | Buy Rs 1,638 add Rs 1,565 | Target Rs 1,980 | Stop loss Rs 1,354 
 Airtel’s operator in Rajasthan and the North East (70% owned by Bharti Airtel) and the market leader in both circles, with revenue shares of 43.4% and 57.9%. EBITDA margin has expanded from 49.2% in FY24 to 54.8% in Q1 FY27, and Q1 net income grew 23.2%. ARPU rose 5.3% to Rs 259, Airtel’s prepaid plan changes add pricing headroom, and home broadband customers grew 83% in a year. Net debt is only 0.2x EBITDAaL and the FY26 dividend rose 80% to Rs 18. Key risks are the overhang of TCIL’s 15% stake, a P/E of about 45x and competition from Jio and Vodafone Idea, highlighted Jainam

 InCred Equities has identified five stocks across healthcare, hospitality, auto ancillaries, online marketplaces and industrial materials, with potential upside of up to 46 percent. These are as follows:
 RHI Magnesita India: Refractories| CMP 364 | Target Price Rs 492 | Upside 35%
 CarTrade Tech: Online marketplaces | CMP 2,493 | Target Price Rs 3,517 | Upside 41%
 Artemis Medicare: Hospitals | CMP 300 | Target Price Rs 437 | Upside 46%
 Rolex Rings: Auto ancillary-forgings | CMP 189 | Target Price Rs 251 | Upside 33%
 Lemon Tree Hotels: Hotels | CMP 115 | Target Price Rs 142 | Upside 23%
